title: Austin Streets & Cemetery Debts Dominate 1887
summary:
• **Street Infrastructure & Bridge Work** – Council approved a contract to widen the bridge on East Cherry Street over Waller Creek after the original contractors abandoned the project. Some aldermen raised concerns about process and proper bidding procedures.

• **Cemetery Debt Crisis** – The city faced a serious financial problem: a $1,000 note to J.H. Pallott for Greenwood Cemetery, due in June, remained unpaid. Mayor Robertson called for immediate action, warning that creditors deserved respect and the city couldn't ignore the obligation.

• **Tight Budget with No Room for Growth** – Finance Committee reported the city would have only $76 left in the treasury by December 1887. Council could make no new appropriations beyond current operating expenses without risking a deficit.

• **Minor Forgiveness & Fines** – Council forgave fines against an elderly resident due to health concerns (contingent on leaving the city), but refused to remit fines against another man for profane language.

• **Public Health Updates** – City Physician reported 146 visits and 202 prescriptions in June; 19 deaths recorded (13 white, 6 colored). Overall health conditions were good for the season.

St. Comtee The Mayor also laid before the City Council E. Cherry St. Communications from
the street committee to the City engineer, which the City engineer had referred to him for
advice and instructions. They were, in substance, as follows: First – Aldermen Graham and
Phillips, of the Committee, instructed the City engineer to notify Mr. Fisher, to whom the
contract for widening the bridge on East Cherry Street, over Waller Creek, - had been
relet, by consent of the bondsmen of the former contractors, they having abandoned their
contract, to begin work on the bridge on July 11, 1887.
Second – Alderman Schuher, Chairman of the Committee, instructed the City engineer to
defer action on the matter, and refer the same to the City Council, for the following
reasons:
That travel on East Cherry Street would
be impossible; that North Avenue. bridge
should be passable for travel before work on East Cherry Street should begin; that the
reletting of the contract without a meeting of the street Committee and City engineer was
not, in his judgment, right; that after the contract was abandoned by the first
contractors, it should have been relet to the lowest and best bidder, as the ordinances of
the City require.
Alderman Fisher moved that the City Council ratify and confirm the contract, and approve
the action of the majority of the street Committee and the ordering of the work to begin.
Adopted.
